      "observations": [
        "Reuse the retained complete31-file historical reading and exact full-diff record, including removed localization strings and changed tests. Fresh reconciliation reads the formatter/control/caller changes needed for the newly complete discussion, the full fixed accepted formatter and all retained selected caller/test windows. No second full dependency or localization-library traversal is claimed.",
        "The landed change replaces constructed date/time/range strings and name helpers with whole Intl-formatting boundaries and zero-based name arrays. InvitationInterval now uses formatItemInterval, recurrence widgets create locale labels with separate one-based values, minimonth uses narrow visible names plus full aria-label names, and numeric year/month attributes remain separate from formatted display. The Today Pane explicitly keeps a raw numeric day for the small CJK-sensitive label while formatting the adjacent month/year.",
        "Current formatter.getItemDates converts item dates to the display timezone and adjusts the exclusive all-day end for display. Date-only/floating values remain user-relative; fixed-zone values use offset-adjusted JS Dates and UTC formatting. These display operations do not change stored event dates. Later accepted additions include explicit timeZone options, date-only formatDateTime handling, month intervals and cache invalidation on intl:app-locales-changed; they are not all introduced by1065. The lazy name-array lifecycle is not proved by clearing the formatter cache.",
        "The actual historical/default source changes intl.regional_prefs.use_os_locales from true to false, and the fixed pin retains false. General preferences hide the real radio fieldset when base languages match outside automation and label the two radio controls otherwise. Its comment describes regional-locale precedence in the matching-language case. This is inspected comm implementation/comment; paired Gecko locale policy and the actual radio preference binding are not independently traced here.",
        "Full Bug1917411 comments0–8 and D221752 timeline/all3 actual Done inline messages are read. They retain Italian/Japanese manual reports, broad locale discussion, proposed feedback/data actions and acceptance after rebase. The author chooses narrow weekday labels; a retained task-interval exception is left in place. Magnus objects to translating names via regional formatting and later explicitly rebuts the author interpretation of low nondefault preference use. There is no consensus that unchanged defaults mean users do not care. Landed false is source evidence, not proof that either telemetry interpretation is correct.",
        "Current interval tests use actual DATE strings for all-day cases, timed values separately and named acceptable Intl variants. The assertion calls expected.includes(formatted); array cases compare member values, while string cases permit substring matching. The test source therefore does not establish strict exact-string equality for every row. Changed invitation/recurrence tests are retained as complete historical proof, with focused changed unit expectations freshly read; no locale, timezone, keyboard or screen-reader test ran.",
        "The current legacy calendar-day-label date setter still calls dayName twice although the full current formatter exposes weekdayNames and no dayName. The historical diff also leaves the long date-setter calls unchanged while updating short names and weekDay. Active reachability of this legacy setter is unestablished; current multiday headings use their own formatter-array calls. This is a scoped interface discrepancy, not a reproduced runtime bug. Later print corrections/regression links are context only and not extra coverage."
